clue.text: Record attempt to suppress second hanging

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down out of sight, so the two outer pieces close over and hide the next one

blocks.note: to tape is to record
S is the abbreviation for second
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone attempting a record has been hushed up, while a second person is left dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: Hanging is the noun, a wall hanging; the container splits the outer pair only where record ends and attempt begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven fabric hung on a wall, so a wall hanging is a fair description of one.

clue.text: Was first to enter extremely Spanish city

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this piece sits within the other

blocks.note: too means excessively, extremely
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: Someone became the first person to get into a thoroughly Spanish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely Spanish' tempts you to take the ends of Spanish; extremely is a word in its own right, and Spanish belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, once its capital.

clue.text: Fruit — it may go off

blocks.note: first meaning: the tropical fruit
second meaning: slang for a hand grenade, which explodes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' suggests fruit rotting, but here it means exploding: the grenade is nicknamed for its segmented shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the tropical fruit and, in military slang, a hand grenade that can detonate.

clue.text: Keep carrying weapons and refuse to compromise?

blocks.note: first meaning, literal: to keep one's firearms close
second meaning: the idiom for standing firm in one's position

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first reading takes the idiom literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stand by one's opinion despite opposition, which is refusing to give ground.

clue.text: Proper shock, female leaving

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: a fright is a shock
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A real scare as a woman walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper shock' reads as British slang for a real shock, but proper is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Right means correct or fitting, as in the proper or right way to do something.

clue.text: An old calculator may make a graduate swear endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word for swear is cut off

blocks.note: taken as written
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
to cuss is to swear

explanation.surface: Struggling with an ancient counting device might drive a graduate to curse without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on wires used for arithmetic long before electronic calculators.

clue.text: New Bled artist's keen to give one pleasure

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters that follow are formed into something different

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A painter newly arrived in Bled, the Slovenian lake resort, is eager to please.
explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is a pub game like ninepins; the phrase is chiefly heard in 'life isn't all beer and skittles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer and skittles is an idiom for carefree enjoyment, which is pleasure.

clue.text: Daily, daughter could bring a vegetable

blocks.note: a daily or char is a cleaning lady
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Each day a daughter might bring home some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like 'every day', but it is a British noun for a cleaner who comes in by day, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green plant related to beet, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Authoritarian English novelist

blocks.note: stern means strict, authoritarian
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A description of a strict, bossy writer from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English novelist' looks like one definition, but English is just E and novelist alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne wrote the eighteenth-century novel Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Writer's article about a depressed US city

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pair of pieces surrounds the next pair

blocks.note: a pen is a writer, with the 's meaning has
a is the indefinite article
taken as written
sad means depressed

explanation.surface: An author's piece about a gloomy American town.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a crossword writer; the possessive 's just glues writer to article, and the outer pair is split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city in California near Los Angeles, home of the Rose Bowl.

clue.text: Slang used to describe popular US city

indicators.note: something used is worn and knocked about, so the word slang gets its letters jumbled
to describe a figure is to draw round it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
something in is fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Colloquial words are applied to portray a well-liked American town.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of slang open up after their fourth letter to wrap around IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lansing is the state capital of Michigan, a city in the United States.

clue.text: Storm following hail is normal

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word for storm is placed second, behind the word for hail

blocks.note: ave is a Latin greeting, a hail
to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: A weather report: a storm coming after a hailstorm is nothing unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the storm piece after the hail piece; hail here is a greeting, not ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Average describes what is typical or ordinary, the same sense as normal.

clue.text: Swallowed drop of daiquiri before row

indicators.note: a drop is the smallest amount, so only the opening letter of the drink is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of daiquiri
a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis

explanation.surface: Someone downed a sip of cocktail just before an argument broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of things, as in a taxi rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Drank is the past tense of drink, meaning swallowed liquid.

clue.text: A red agent murdered in restaurant

indicators.note: something murdered is mangled, so the letters before it are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A spy-thriller scene: a communist agent is killed while dining out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor café or eating place serving tea and light meals, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Fellow grasping nothing at university? Revision is required

indicators.note: grasping means holding in the hand, so the fellow's word goes around the nothing

blocks.note: a professor, as in a college fellow
O looks like zero, nothing
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: An academic who has achieved nothing at university needs to be reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage one reads a subject at university, so 'at university' gives READING.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreading is checking and correcting a text, a form of revision before printing.

clue.text: Five sat out, then left for jamboree

indicators.note: out means disordered or not in place, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Five people sat out, then went off to a big Scout gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large celebration or gathering, which is what a festival is.

clue.text: Film noir, too grim — American

indicators.note: grim suggests something ugly and twisted, so the letters before it are distorted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict: an American dark thriller that is overly bleak.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious is a 1946 Hitchcock spy thriller starring Cary Grant and Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Scam at Wimbledon? This could help one make a good return

definitions.text: This could help one make a good return

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: a racket (a swindle) in the world of tennis

blocks.clueFragment: This could help one make a good return
blocks.note: second meaning: the strung bat used to hit a ball back over the net

explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the famous London tennis tournament; a racket is both a swindle and a bat, and a return is hitting the ball back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the strung frame a player swings, while racket also means a fraud, hence the scam reading.

clue.text: Credit is doubled for use in emergency

blocks.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit
the word is, written twice

explanation.surface: Your credit limit is doubled to be used in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubled' is an instruction to write the word is twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty, which is an emergency.

clue.text: County town originally producing wine

indicators.note: originally means at the origin or start, so just the opening letter is used

blocks.note: Clare is a county in the west of Ireland
the opening letter of town

explanation.surface: A provincial town that first began making wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County town' reads as one phrase, a county's administrative centre, but county and town are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Touching, calling for pardon

blocks.note: re means regarding, touching on
a mission is a vocation or calling

explanation.surface: A moving plea, appealing for forgiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' looks like 'moving', but it is the sense 'concerning', abbreviated RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is the forgiveness of sins or cancellation of a penalty, the same idea as a pardon.

clue.text: Copper, and others, after leader of mob?

indicators.note: the leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of mob
et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: A policeman and his colleagues chase down a gang boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer chasing the mob, but it is the element; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a metal, so it defines the answer by example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Chemist opening in Bury during Christmas

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its start, so only its first letter is used
during means within a period, so the letter is placed inside the season's word

blocks.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
the opening letter of Bury

explanation.surface: A pharmacy opening in the Lancashire town of Bury over the Christmas period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chemist' suggests a British pharmacy shop, but it is a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, inventor of dynamite and founder of the Nobel Prizes, was a Swedish chemist.

clue.text: Some nifty rollerblading in Austrian province

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of nifty and the start of rollerblading

explanation.surface: Someone shows off clever skating moves in an Alpine region.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrol is a state of western Austria in the Alps, so an Austrian province.

clue.text: Fruit, a necessity over in South Africa

indicators.note: turned over means read the other way, so the phrase before it runs backwards

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
a must is a necessity

explanation.surface: In South Africa a certain fruit is considered essential.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a kind of mandarin orange, a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Former PM (Labour) turned back on a number

indicators.note: turned back means facing the other way, so the party's short form is read backwards

blocks.note: Lab is the short form of Labour, the British political party
four is a number

explanation.surface: A former Labour prime minister changed position on some figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed Labour pretends to be the PM's party; Balfour was a Conservative, and Labour is just letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour was British Prime Minister from 1902 to 1905, so a past holder of that office.

clue.text: Hack holding page with prominent headline

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so the word for hack wraps around the page

blocks.note: to hack is to slash
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A journalist hogs a whole page with a big front-page story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a journalist, fitting the newspaper scene, but it is the verb to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: In newspaper jargon a splash is the main front-page story, run under large, eye-catching type.

clue.text: Located near each other, residential streets, extremely elegant

indicators.note: at the extremes of the word, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: a close is a cul-de-sac of houses
the first and last letters of elegant

explanation.surface: An estate agent's blurb: neighbouring houses on smart cul-de-sacs.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a close is a short residential street, often a dead end.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-set describes things placed tightly together, such as close-set eyes.
